items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: I think Cottrell made one or two arrangements. Herbert Hall made some.

ctx.x: Tim came up with something about arrangements. Did you pay the men to do arrangements?

We didn't have any money to pay ourselves nothing. Would you have a bond for everybody in the band? Well, everybody in the band worked as a family. That's what it was. If we made ten dollars, we'd split ten dollars. By the same token, if we made a hundred, we'd split a hundred. And everybody wanted the band to be the best and everybody would chip in the things that they knew how. I think Cottrell made one or two arrangements. Herbert Hall made some. And of course we had Harold Holmes, who did a tremendous job of…

items.title: Don Albert and Herbert Hall Interview, 1978-08-03
items.q: The band was organized in the audience. That's how we left, Julian. And, uh, Don had a job in Dallas at the States.

ctx.x: What was it like when you joined the band? Where is it? Were you all alone? Were you all alone? Were you all alone? Were you all alone? playing occasionally on a record, but not big bands apparently. Right. Not that I just like the one I've heard. It is, it is. I just wondered why I looked at it. What was it like when you joined the band? Where?
We all left in the audience together. You all left in the audience? The band was organized in the audience. That's how we left, Julian. And, uh, Don had a job in Dallas at the States.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-09-18
items.q: And, well, we had Arthur Durbney and Herb Hall, those are the original members, Alvin Martin.

ctx.x: Yeah. That's his boy. And, well, we had Arthur Durbney and Herb Hall, those are the original members, Alvin Martin. No one with a great education by no reason. But they were very intelligent and very well behaved. Beautiful. Beautiful. Everyone I meet from that band. Well, they didn't, one thing, they didn't drink. I didn't have one in that I could consider a drinker.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-05-11
items.q: gave it to Herbert Hall. It was my clarinetist and also my alto man.

ctx.x: Someday we might want to do that if we don't find the originals.

Well, I have an original of the Shadowland Blues, the one that was made with Troy Floyd, and I played a solo on the other side. And I have also a master record on one of these numbers. I think it's True Blue Lou. But the other is a copy from a jazz enthusiast that picked it up in Europe and gave it to Herbert Hall. It was my clarinetist and also my alto man.
Oh, it's Herbert Hall. Is that the brother of Edmund Hall? That's correct.
